articles.title: Adventures of a Stargazer
articles.summary: This article recounts various unexpected and often humorous misadventures experienced by an amateur astronomer, Lee Hoglan, while pursuing stargazing and observatory building. From confusing authorities about his equipment and construction projects to rescuing horses from an accident and searching for his father's lost dentures, the anecdotes highlight the less glamorous but memorable sides of an astronomer's life. Despite these challenges, the author shares the unique experiences that come with the hobby.

articles.title: SJAA Yosemite Star Party
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its annual Yosemite Star Party at Glacier Point on July 25-26. Up to 30 participants will receive free admission and camping in exchange for leading public stargazing events on both evenings. This event, prioritizing SJAA members, offers rough camping conditions and coincides with a new moon for optimal viewing.

articles.title: Big-Bang Theory: New Evidence
articles.summary: Scientists announced in March 2014 the discovery of indirect evidence for gravitational waves from the earliest moments of the universe, offering strong support for the cosmic inflation theory. This evidence comes from detecting a unique 'B-mode' polarization pattern in the cosmic microwave background using the BICEP2 telescope. If confirmed, this finding would be a monumental discovery, providing the oldest evidence of the universe's initial expansion, occurring a tiny fraction of a second after the Big Bang.

articles.title: Hubble Witnesses Asteroid's Mysterious Disintegration
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has documented the unprecedented disintegration of asteroid P/2013 R3 into as many as 10 smaller fragments within the asteroid belt. This slow, mysterious breakup, distinct from comets or collision events, is attributed to a subtle effect of sunlight gradually increasing the asteroid's rotation, causing its weakly structured interior to pull apart due to centrifugal force. The observation provides crucial evidence for a previously theorized mechanism of asteroid destruction, contributing to our understanding of small asteroid evolution and future meteoroid sources.

articles.title: KID SPOT
articles.summary: This 'Kid Spot' article provides engaging astronomy content, including space-themed jokes and a quiz. It features a 'Night Sky Challenge' for March 2014, highlighting celestial objects like Jupiter, Mars, and a total lunar eclipse. The main educational section offers a detailed exploration of the constellation Leo, discussing its mythology, prominent stars, and notable deep-sky objects, alongside its historical significance.

articles.title: Club Updates
articles.summary: This SJAA 'Club Updates' article details several member services and upcoming events. It announces the SJAA library's recent makeover, a wishlist for children's books, and accepts donations and feedback. It also highlights the Advanced Loaner Telescope Program for equipment evaluation, the Fix-It Program for repairs, and lists key upcoming events including the Cupertino Earth Day Festival, Astronomy Day, the Yosemite Star Party, and the Golden State Star Party. Additionally, there is an open board seat available.

articles.title: Board Meeting Excerpts March 15, 2014
articles.summary: The Board Meeting Excerpts from March 15, 2014, detail the selection of 2014 officers, including Rob Jaworski as President. Key upcoming events discussed include an In-Town Start Party at Bear Creek Stables on April 4th and a Total Lunar Eclipse Party scheduled for April 14-15. Additionally, plans were made to generate an announcement regarding a new book wish list for the Club library.

articles.title: SJAA Auction 2014
articles.summary: The 34th annual SJAA Auction was a significant success, generating over $6700 in transactions from approximately 50 bidders and 10 sellers for more than 100 lots, netting the club over $2600. The event, which ran smoothly with food and entertainment provided by new auctioneer Greg Claytor, brought substantial value to the amateur astronomy community in the Bay Area and Northern California.
